data.etymology: Avadhut belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Freedom from worldly attachments.”

data.cultural_impact: The name Avadhut holds great respect in Hindu culture as it signifies a person who has dedicated their life to spiritual pursuits and renounced worldly attachments. Avadhut is often portrayed as an exemplar of selflessness, bravery, and spiritual strength. In Hindu mythology, stories of Avadhuts are told to inspire devotion and to provide lessons on the importance of detachment and spiritual growth.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Avadhut signifies a deep level of inner transformation and realization of the ultimate truth. The person named Avadhut has transcended ordinary life and has achieved a state of profound detachment from material desires and worldly pursuits. They have attained a state of spiritual freedom and have realized the true nature of the universe. This name serves as a constant reminder of the importance of inner growth and the pursuit of spiritual enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Avadhut, meaning 'the one who has renounced all desires and attachments', symbolizes detachment and self-realization in Hinduism. His heart is filled with pure devotion towards the divine, and his mind is free from worldly distractions.
